data.name: Malcolm
data.gender_notes: Malcolm is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Scottish Gaelic 'Máel Coluim'. Máel means 'disciple' or 'servant', and Coluim is 'columba', which means 'dove'. In Scottish history, Malcolm has been borne by several significant figures, including two kings. The name Malcolm carries the meaning “Rule of the gentle” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Malcolm usually hope their child will grow to embody rule of the gentle and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Malcolm belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rule of the gentle.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Malcolm total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Malcolm has been prominent in Scottish history and culture, with several kings, warriors, and notable individuals carrying the name. Malcolm Canmore, who ruled Scotland from 1058 to 1097, is one such figure. Additionally, Malcolm Murray from the X-Men in Marvel Comics has gained popular recognition. The name has a sense of strength and power associated with it.
data.spiritual_significance: Malcolm's meaning as 'disciple' or 'servant' roots the name in the spiritual realm, reminding one of their role as a devoted follower and servant of God. The inclusion of Columba, meaning dove, symbolizes peace, purity, and the Holy Spirit. Overall, the name embodies a firm faith and dedication to one's beliefs.
